payload.body:
You notice quickly when another person has more control over the situation than you do. They decide when you get access, hold information you need, control money tied to the decision, change the terms, or have enough influence that your options start depending on what they are willing to allow.

Once you see the imbalance, it can be hard to leave it alone. You want the explanation, the correction, or some acknowledgement that the other person knows what they are doing. The more they avoid the issue, the more determined you can become to make the situation clear.

The problem is that the struggle can start taking up more of your life than the original problem. You send another message, gather more evidence, replay what happened, or keep trying to get someone to admit something their behavior has already shown you.

Control is not the same as safety. You do not need them to admit what happened before you decide what you will do next. Sometimes the most useful thing you can do with the truth is stop giving the situation more access to your time, attention, money, or energy.
